name: Weller Special Reserve

facts.base: A wheated bourbon mash: corn, with wheat in place of rye, and malted barley
facts.age: No age statement; as a straight bourbon without one, at least four years
facts.law: Kentucky straight bourbon: at least 51 per cent corn, new charred oak, at least two years

made: Weller is distilled at Buffalo Trace in Frankfort from a wheated bourbon mash: corn first, then wheat where most bourbons use rye, and a little malted barley. The distillery does not publish the proportions, and the same wheated recipe goes into the Van Winkle bourbons. The spirit rests in new charred American oak in the distillery's warehouses. Special Reserve, the first step of the Weller range, carries no age statement, which for a straight bourbon means at least four years, and it is bottled at 90 proof.
taste: Soft and sweet: honey, caramel and vanilla on the nose, with a little fresh bread from the wheat. The palate is light to medium, butterscotch and toffee with a touch of orange peel and gentle oak, and none of the pepper a rye recipe brings. The finish is short, sweet and warm.

lines.s10: Weller Special Reserve is a wheated Kentucky straight bourbon from Buffalo Trace: soft honey and caramel, gentle and sweet, at 90 proof.
lines.s20: Weller Special Reserve is a Kentucky straight bourbon made at Buffalo Trace with wheat in place of rye, the style its label calls the original wheated bourbon. The wheat makes it soft and round: honey, caramel and vanilla, with no peppery bite, at 90 proof.
lines.s45: This is Weller Special Reserve, which its label calls the original wheated bourbon. It is a Kentucky straight bourbon distilled at Buffalo Trace in Frankfort from corn, wheat and malted barley: wheat takes the place of rye, so the spice steps back. It rests in new charred American oak and is bottled at 90 proof. Expect honey, caramel and vanilla, then a soft, round palate of butterscotch and gentle oak, and a short, sweet finish. We pour it neat or over one large cube, and it makes a gentle Old Fashioned. It carries the name of William Larue Weller, a Louisville whiskey merchant from 1849.
lines.sale: Weller Special Reserve is the soft side of bourbon: wheat instead of rye, so it is all honey and caramel with no bite. Try it over one large cube, or in an Old Fashioned for a guest who finds bourbon too sharp.

serve.neat: Neat at room temperature; a drop of water lifts the honey.
serve.rocks: Over one large cube; at 90 proof it softens quickly, so it goes out as soon as it is poured.
serve.glass: A Glencairn or a small tulip neat; a rocks glass for the cube or the Old Fashioned.
serve.classic: An Old Fashioned or a Whiskey Sour; its softness also suits a Mint Julep or a Gold Rush.

guest: Weller Special Reserve is a Kentucky bourbon made with wheat instead of rye, so it is soft and sweet: honey, caramel and vanilla, at 90 proof.
story: The bourbon carries the name of William Larue Weller. Born in Kentucky in 1825, he went into the whiskey trade in Louisville in 1849 with his younger brother, selling bourbon under the family name, and the brand credits him with putting wheat in the mash where others used rye, though historians still debate whether he distilled it himself. In 1893 his firm hired a young salesman, Pappy Van Winkle, and after Prohibition the Stitzel-Weller Distillery that Van Winkle helped found opened near Louisville in 1935 and made the wheated recipe its own. Weller is distilled today at Buffalo Trace in Frankfort.
watch: Not Weller 12, the black label beside it: the same wheated recipe aged twelve years, deeper and oakier. Special Reserve is the green label.
A guest who asks for a wheater or a soft bourbon wants this; a guest who wants rye spice in a bourbon wants another bottle.
Not Weller Antique 107, the same recipe at 107 proof: read the label, which says Special Reserve and 90 proof.
Asked its age: no age statement; as a straight bourbon without one, it has rested at least four years.

recall.prompt: What is Weller Special Reserve made from, and how strong is it?
recall.answer: A Kentucky straight bourbon from Buffalo Trace in Frankfort, made from corn, wheat and malted barley: wheat in place of rye, the wheated style, which makes it soft, with honey, caramel and vanilla. No age statement, so at least four years; 45% ABV, 90 proof.

quiz.q: Which grain takes the place of rye in the mash of Weller Special Reserve?
quiz.explain: Wheat: Weller is a wheated bourbon of corn, wheat and malted barley, which is why it is soft and sweet rather than spicy.

quiz.q: At what strength is Weller Special Reserve bottled?
quiz.explain: 90 proof, 45% ABV. Weller Antique 107 is the same wheated recipe at 107 proof.

quiz.q: In which city did William Larue Weller go into the whiskey trade in 1849?
quiz.explain: Louisville, with his younger brother. The bourbon that carries his name is distilled today at Buffalo Trace in Frankfort.
